blocks.title: Commercial Engine
blocks.body: JW Marriott commercial distribution rides Marriott Bonvoy direct channels, GDS, OTAs, and parent sales systems. Luxury full-service: polished public spaces, elevated F&B, and Marriott Bonvoy distribution for travelers seeking classic luxury with modern service. Owners should underwrite channel mix and loyalty contribution for this asset—not corporate averages alone.

blocks.title: Marriott Bonvoy
blocks.body: JW Marriott participates in Marriott Bonvoy. Members earn and redeem points and receive Elite recognition across participating sister brands. Confirm current tier names and earn rules on the official program site before IC.

blocks.title: Loyalty
blocks.body: Marriott Bonvoy at JW Marriott

blocks.title: Earn
blocks.body: Guests earn Marriott Bonvoy points on qualifying stays at JW Marriott. Elite members may receive enhanced earn and recognition benefits per current program rules.

blocks.title: Redeem
blocks.body: Points redeem for stays across the Marriott Bonvoy portfolio, including JW Marriott, subject to availability and current redemption charts.

blocks.title: Elite Recognition
blocks.body: Elite status recognition (upgrades, late checkout, lounge access where offered) applies per property capability—delivery varies by hotel.

blocks.title: Ecosystem
blocks.body: Marriott Bonvoy partnerships, co-branded cards, and bonus campaigns expand the loyalty halo; JW Marriott stays remain the property-level earn/redeem node.

blocks.title: Owner Lens
blocks.body: Marriott Bonvoy drives distribution and repeat demand but adds loyalty chargebacks and program economics. Underwrite net contribution after loyalty—not membership vanity metrics.

blocks.body: Loyalty assessments and program contribution affect net rooms revenue. Use current agreement exhibits; do not invent undisclosed rates.

blocks.title: Operating Implications
blocks.body: Front desk and systems must support Marriott Bonvoy enrollment, Elite recognition, and redemption stays without erasing the brand's guest experience.

blocks.title: Systems Implications
blocks.body: Parent property and reservation systems integration is required for Marriott Bonvoy participation—budget cutover and training in the conversion plan.

blocks.title: Repeat Guest Capture
blocks.body: Marriott Bonvoy earn and recognition increase the probability of repeat JW Marriott stays where the hotel already competes on product fit—not on a standardized prototype alone.

blocks.title: Direct Channel & Member Pricing
blocks.body: Bonvoy member rates and Marriott direct paths help JW Marriott hotels defend contribution against high-commission intermediaries while keeping brand positioning intact.

blocks.title: Elite Member Value
blocks.body: Elite recognition (upgrades where available, late checkout, milestone rewards) supports contribution at JW Marriott; amenity delivery still varies by property capability.

blocks.title: Cross-Brand Traveler Flow
blocks.body: Bonvoy recognition across Marriott sister brands matters for guests who split stays within the network—JW Marriott remains the brand-specific node inside that earn/redeem graph.

blocks.body: Bonvoy co-branded cards, Moments, and bonus-point campaigns lift acquisition; model hotel-level contribution after loyalty chargebacks—not portfolio vanity metrics.

blocks.body: Marriott account linkage and negotiated transient patterns support midweek compression where corporate and SMERF mix fits the JW Marriott asset—confirm for this hotel's source markets.

blocks.title: When Things Change
blocks.body: Renewal PIP; conversion PIP revisions; transfer / change-of-ownership fees; termination-related obligations; owner-funded reserves—triggered at renewal, repositioning, or exit. Confirm liquidated damages and transfer mechanics in the current agreement.

blocks.title: Why Value Is Strongest in These Scenarios
blocks.body:
Keep Local Product Intent—Add Marriott Bonvoy: retain JW Marriott's brand promise while accessing loyalty earn/redeem and parent commercial systems a standalone hotel cannot buy alone.
Luxury full-service: polished public spaces, elevated F&B, and Marriott Bonvoy distribution for travelers seeking classic luxury with modern service.
Sibling Clarity: diligence fit versus same-parent peers before assuming identical owner use case or fee path.
Operator & Owner Fit: strongest when the asset can deliver the brand's guest promise with QA discipline—weakest when sponsors want the flag without the product investment.
Disclosure Discipline: model economics only from current fee exhibits—Factory 2.0 does not invent undisclosed percentages.
